commitResults.messageBody:
The feedback box was fixed at 62 to 90 pixels, so a message with a
command's usage showed two lines and a scroll bar. Feedback is how
users learn whether a command worked, so it should be readable at a
glance.

Let's grow the box with its message, from one line up to six. Only
longer messages scroll, and short ones leave more room for the screen
above.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md for AI agents
commitResults.messageBody:
AI coding agents used by team members do not know the course
constraints, the Java and Git conventions, or the PR workflow, so
their output can violate graded requirements.

Let's add AGENTS.md describing those rules, and a CLAUDE.md that
imports it. Stop ignoring both files so that they are shared with
the whole team.

Feature tests need students with sensible defaults instead of
each test constructing names and IDs by hand.

Build a group with a default name and any number of students. Each
build() returns a new Group, so tests never share a mutable group.

Share one set of students across tests. Two extra students are
kept outside the typical list for tests that add a new student.

Provide typical groups T01, T02 and T03, which have three, two and
no students. Group is mutable, so each getter returns a new group
to stop tests from affecting one another.

Build a TAssist from groups and an optional active group. The active
group is set when build() is called, so it may be named before its
group is added.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add typical TAssist data to TypicalGroups
commitResults.messageBody:

commitResults.messageBody:

active group, and copying an existing TAssist.
Drop the students that the test built by hand.

Drop the students that the test built by hand, and build the
same-ID student with StudentBuilder.
Drop the group name and students that the test built by hand.

Create a new typical group for each test, so that a test cannot
change a group that another test uses.

Start from the typical TAssist instead of adding groups and students
by hand in every test, and use TAssistBuilder to set the active group.

Tell developers which builders and typical data exist, and why the
mutable ones must be created fresh in every test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a JSON adapter for students
commitResults.messageBody:
The TAssist data file needs to hold each student's name and ID, and a
wrong manual edit to either must be reported rather than crash the app.

Let's add a Jackson-friendly student that checks both fields when it is
turned back into a Student.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a JSON adapter for tutorial groups
commitResults.messageBody:
Each tutorial group in the data file holds its name and its students.
A manual edit may leave out the student list, add an empty entry, or
repeat a student ID within the group.

Let's add a Jackson-friendly group that reads a missing student list as
no students, and rejects empty entries and repeated student IDs with a
message naming the group.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a JSON form of the whole TAssist data
commitResults.messageBody:
The data file holds every tutorial group and which group is active. A
manual edit may repeat a group name in a different case, name an active
group that does not exist, or leave out either field.

Let's add a serializable TAssist that reads a missing group list as no
groups and a missing active group as none, and rejects repeated group
names and an unknown active group with a specific message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JSON file storage for TAssist data
commitResults.messageBody:
TAssist data lives only in memory, so tutorial groups and students are
lost when the app closes.

Let's add a storage class that saves TAssist data to a JSON file and
reads it back, reporting a missing file as no data and an unreadable or
invalid file as a loading error.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let Storage read and save TAssist data
commitResults.messageBody:
The JSON storage for TAssist data is not reachable through the Storage
component, so Logic and the app launcher cannot use it.

Let's give Storage methods to read and save TAssist data, and keep the
TAssist data file at data/tassist.json.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save TAssist data after each command
commitResults.messageBody:
Successful commands save AddressBook data, so changes to tutorial
groups, students and the active group are lost when the app closes.

Let's save TAssist data instead, so the data file follows every
successful command other than view. A failed save is still reported to
the user.

commitResults.messageTitle: Load TAssist data from the data file at startup
commitResults.messageBody:
Every run starts with no tutorial groups, and a first launch fills the
app with sample contacts.

Let's restore groups, students and the active group from the TAssist
data file when the app starts. A missing file starts an empty TAssist
with no sample data, and an unreadable or invalid file starts an empty
TAssist and logs why the file could not be read. AddressBook data is no
longer loaded.

commitResults.messageTitle: Stop wiring AddressBook storage into Storage
commitResults.messageBody:
The app no longer reads or saves AddressBook data, so the AddressBook
methods of Storage are unused.

Let's remove them from Storage and StorageManager. The AddressBook
storage classes stay until the AddressBook code is removed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe TAssist data on the Storage screen
commitResults.messageBody:
The Storage screen says contact commands are saved and a first launch
shows sample contacts, which is no longer true.

Let's say that tutorial groups and students are saved and that a first
launch starts empty.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe the TAssist data file in the UG
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG says contact data is saved to data/addressbook.json and that a
first launch shows sample data, which is no longer true.

Let's describe what TAssist saves, where the data file is, what it
looks like, and what happens when it is missing or invalid.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show TAssist storage in the storage class diagram
commitResults.messageBody:
The storage class diagram shows AddressBook storage, which Storage no
longer uses.

Let's show the TAssist storage classes in its place.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe saving and loading TAssist data in the DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG says TAssist data is not saved and describes AddressBook
storage, and its manual tests expect sample contacts on first launch.

Let's describe the TAssist data file, how it is saved and loaded, how
later features add their own records to it, and how to test a missing
or invalid file by hand.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test loading TAssist data at startup
commitResults.messageBody:
Loading the data file at startup has no tests, so a regression in how
a missing, valid or invalid file is handled would go unnoticed.

Let's make the model setup in MainApp visible to tests in its package,
and test each of the three cases.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject a data file that holds only null
commitResults.messageBody:
A data file whose whole content is null makes JsonUtil return
Optional.of(null), which throws NullPointerException and crashes the
app at startup instead of starting with an empty TAssist.

Let's treat such a file as unreadable, so it is reported like any other
invalid file. This also covers the preferences file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Quote the active group name in load errors
commitResults.messageBody:
When the active group in the data file is blank, the error reads "The
active group  is not in the group list.", which hides what is wrong.

Let's quote the name, so a blank or space-padded name is visible.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tidy TAssist storage Javadoc and message names
commitResults.messageBody:
One saveTAssist overload documents only one of its two parameters, and
the group adapter names its missing-field message differently from the
student adapter.

Let's document both parameters and use the student adapter's naming
for the group's missing-field message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check why rejected TAssist files are rejected
commitResults.messageBody:
Some storage tests only check that an invalid file is rejected, so they
would still pass if it were rejected for the wrong reason.

Let's also check the reason, and name the active group test after both
things it covers.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mention the active group on the Storage screen
commitResults.messageBody:
The Storage screen lists tutorial groups and students as saved data,
but the active group is saved too.

Let's restore the UG's earlier wording about failed commands, and say

init() always reads preferences.json and data/tassist.json, so a
test cannot start the app without touching the real files.

Let a package-private constructor supply those paths. The public
constructor still uses the same default files.

The TAssist startup, UI start and shutdown log lines in MainApp are
not executed by the existing tests.

- Start MainApp from temporary files and check the loaded data
- Check that start hands the stage to the UI
- Check that stop writes the user preferences
Add shared weekly record mechanism

commitResults.messageTitle: Drop participation from coming soon notes
commitResults.messageBody:
Participation set and list are implemented, so Help and
Storage should not say those commands are still planned.

The linked mock-up shows only the Attendance screen.
Students, Help, Storage, and the group bar already use
live data, while four screens are still previews.

AttendanceStatus.fromValue throws for any stored status
other than present or absent, and that exception is not
turned into command feedback.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject invalid participation scores on load
commitResults.messageBody:
A hand-edited score outside 0-5 was kept and listed,
while participation set rejects it. Reject it on load
the same way an invalid week is rejected.
